niche.habitat: Shallow tidal karst shelves and hyphal-overburdened basalt plains
niche.diet: Chitin-glucan rhizomorphs, detrital slurry, carbonate minerals, opportunistic carrion
niche.active: Crepuscular and diurnal (tracks low-UV bands, avoids thermal peak)

body: Broad, flattened carapace; laterally angled legs; asymmetrical chelae; ventrally tucked abdomen; low sensory antennae; melanin-streaked edges

chains.trait: Broad, flattened carapace fused to thoracic segments
links: Reduces tipping on slick fungal substrates
Minimizes profile in dense karst fissures
Shields ventral organs from crushing debris
Driven by 1.2g gravity and pervasive basalt-karst terrain

skill.effect: Reduces incoming damage by 30% and grants 2 turns of cover.

chains.weakness: Vulnerable to top-down strikes and high-impact blows that exploit the broad profile.
observe: Glossy dorsal plate fused to body

journal.en: Why flat? Gravity and stone demand it.

plausibility.summary: Under 1.2g (F3), a low, wide exoskeleton lowers the center of mass and contact stress on slick, uneven karst–hyphal substrates (F10). A fused dorsal shield protects against abrasive particulate load in the 15 m visibility regime (F8) and matches chitin–glucan armour chemistry (F13). Fused thoracic shields are standard in many pancrustacean-grade lineages; convergent flattening appears in unrelated terrestrial arthropods under similar ‘don’t roll off the rock’ selection.

Fused thoracic shields are standard in many pancrustacean-grade lineages; convergent flattening appears in unrelated terrestrial arthropods under similar ‘don’t roll off the rock’ selection.

analogues.organism: Terrestrial isopods (Oniscus, Porcellio)—dorsally flattened tergal plates for crevice stability; horseshoe crab (Limulus)—broad fused prosomal carapace over soft ventral structures.
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Aligns body axis with narrow karst fissures
Reduces joint stress on jagged basalt floors
Evolved from vertical-climbing ancestors reoriented for ground-hugging travel

skill.effect: Moves sideways at full speed without turning penalty; navigates gaps 0.5m wide.

chains.weakness: Struggles on smooth vertical surfaces; blind-side vulnerable.
observe: Never turns broadside to open space

journal.en: They don't march; they sidestep fate.

plausibility.summary: State explicitly that Lombardo’s ancestors were already arthropod-grade with regionalized thorax and paired appendages; ‘12 arms’ = six bilateral pairs of thoracic walking appendages plus chelae (tagmosis), not a novel limb inventory. Soft-ped ancestral vertical climbing can persist as the stated weakness on smooth vertical karst.

analogues.organism: Brachyuran and anomuran ‘crabs’ (multiple carcinisation events); coconut crab (Birgus latro)—terrestrial sideways gait on rough terrain; some lithobiomorph centipedes—lateral undulation in cracks (partial analogue for fissure travel, not crab gait).
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: Ventrally tucked, segmented abdomen beneath carapace
links: Shields soft gills and reproductive ducts in dusty karst
Streamlines rear for sliding into hollows
Prevents snagging on hyphal cords under 1.2g
Maintains low center of gravity during rapid retreats

skill.effect: Retract abdomen to seal ventral side, granting camouflage and reducing detection by 50% while stationary.

chains.weakness: Immobility while tucked; slow recovery time.
observe: Gill rakers visible only when breathing

journal.en: A folded ledger of eggs and gills, kept close.

plausibility.summary: Tidal karst shelves expose ventral respiratory and reproductive surfaces to drying, dust, and debris when mats retract. Retracting a segmented abdomen under the carapace is a mechanical solution that also tucks presumed book-gill or gill-raker surfaces—consistent with semi-aquatic grazing next to anoxic sediments (F11) and particulate haze (F8). Low CoG aids rapid retreat along the ground plane at 1.2g.

analogues.organism: Decapod crabs—abdomen flexed beneath cephalothorax; woodlice (Armadillidium)—conglobation protects ventral appendices and pleopods (stronger analogue for ‘tuck while stationary’).

journal.en: Why claws? Stone and fungus demand both keys and hammers.

body_plan.origin: Highly speculative convergence: terrestrial gravity and karst topography mimic crustacean benthic pressures, driving independent evolution of a craboid form from vertical-climbing detritivore ancestors.

secrets: Their crushed chitin-glucan paste can be harvested to craft temporary enzymatic coatings that accelerate fungal growth.
They avoid hydrothermal vent plumes not from heat, but because geothermal H₂S disrupts their chemical antennae navigation.
During the 600-day apogee, their carapaces molt simultaneously, leaving hollow shells that resonate at 340 m/s when wind passes through.
moments: At low tide, when the fungal mats retract and the karst dries, a hundred Lombardo cluster in the exposed fissures. Their tucked abdomens rise and fall in unison, a slow, chitinous breathing that echoes like distant rain.

journal.en: A broad-shelled detritivore that navigates fungal karst with practiced lateral grace.
Carcinisation? Evolution really does have a favorite body plan.
